cues.en: Instructor: Now that you know all about the measures of central tenancy, the mean, the median, and the mode, it is time to learn about the measures of dispersion.
cues.zh: 既然知道平均、中位數與眾數這些集中趨勢量，該學離散程度的量了。

cues.en: And in particular, I'm going to focus on the dominant measure of dispersion, which is variance.
cues.zh: 特別會聚焦最主要的量，也就是變異數。

cues.en: And I'll talk quite a lot about variance and the formula and what it means and why the formula has to be the way it is.
cues.zh: 會花很多時間談變異數、公式、意義，以及為何公式必須如此。

cues.en: And then I'm gonna spend probably not even 30 seconds talking about standard deviation.
cues.zh: 接著大概不到30秒，談標準差。

cues.en: And towards the end of the video, I'm going to introduce you to a couple of measures that are sometimes used that are a combination of variance and standard deviation and mean,
cues.zh: 影片最後，介紹幾種有時使用，結合變異數、標準差與平均值的量，

cues.en: those are the Fano factor and the coefficient of variation.
cues.zh: 也就是Fano因子與變異係數。

cues.en: So let's get started.
cues.zh: 開始吧。

cues.en: I've already shown you a slide that looks something like this.
cues.zh: 之前展示過類似的投影片。

cues.en: The idea of dispersion is we need a measure of how spread out these different distributions are.
cues.zh: 離散程度的概念，是要衡量不同分布有多分散。

cues.en: So we would...
cues.zh: 所以我們會……

cues.en: We need a single number that we can use to apply to a dataset that tells us how dispersed the data are whatever is the central tendency.
cues.zh: 需要一個能套用到資料集的數字，告訴我們，不論集中趨勢在哪裡，資料有多分散。

cues.en: So this green distribution here should have a smaller number or measure of dispersion, and the blue distribution should have a larger number because these data are more distributed,
cues.zh: 綠色分布的離散程度應該較小，藍色應該較大，因為它的資料分布，

cues.en: more widely distributed compared to this green distribution.
cues.zh: 比綠色更廣。

cues.en: So that's the visualization, that's the idea.
cues.zh: 這就是視覺與概念。

cues.en: And now we get to the main formula.
cues.zh: 現在進入主要公式。

cues.en: So this is a formula for variance.
cues.zh: 這是變異數公式。

cues.en: It's often indicated as sigma square.
cues.zh: 通常寫σ平方。

cues.en: This is the Greek letter sigma.
cues.zh: 這是希臘字母Sigma。

cues.en: Sometimes people use sigma only to indicate population variance, and they'll use the letter S to indicate sample variance.
cues.zh: 有時只用σ表示母體變異數，S表示樣本變異數。

cues.en: So S squared would be sample variance, but not everyone follows that convention.
cues.zh: 所以S平方是樣本變異數，但不是每個人都遵守。

cues.en: You'll also see the sigma squared used for sample variance, which is actually the formula that I'm showing here.
cues.zh: 也會看到σ平方用於樣本變異數，這裡展示的其實就是這種公式。

cues.en: I'll get into that in a little bit.
cues.zh: 稍後說明。

cues.en: So you can see that at first glance, it actually looks a little bit like the formula for the mean, in the sense that we are summing up
cues.zh: 乍看有點像平均公式，因為也是加總，

cues.en: all of the data values and then dividing by n.
cues.zh: 所有資料值，再除以n。

cues.en: So it's not exactly the formula for the mean, we have some things here that make it different.
cues.zh: 但不完全一樣，有些差異。

cues.en: So we divide by n minus one, and we subtract the mean first and then square the values.
cues.zh: 除以n−1，而且先減平均，再平方。

cues.en: So here's the formula for the...
cues.zh: 這是……

cues.en: Here's how this formula works.
cues.zh: 公式運作如下。

cues.en: You take each individual value, each individual data point, and you subtract the mean, this is called mean centering.
cues.zh: 每個個別值、資料點，減去平均，叫平均中心化。

cues.en: And then you square that difference.
cues.zh: 再把差平方。

cues.en: So you take the...
cues.zh: 取這個……

cues.en: That difference to the power of two, and then you sum all of those values together.
cues.zh: 差的2次方，再把所有值加總。

cues.en: And then you divide by n minus one, where n is the number of data points in your sample.
cues.zh: 除以n−1，n是樣本資料點數量。

cues.en: So variance is suitable for any distribution, but it's most easy to interpret for unimodal distributions that are roughly Gaussian distributed.
cues.zh: 變異數適合任何分布，但對大致高斯的單峰分布，最容易解讀。

cues.en: It can be used for any numerical data type.
cues.zh: 任何數值資料類型都能使用。

cues.en: And similar to how the mean is possible to compute on ordinal data, but can be a little bit tricky to interpret, same thing with the variance.
cues.zh: 和次序資料可以算平均、卻稍難解讀類似，變異數也一樣。

cues.en: So you can compute the variance of ordinal data, but it's a little bit...
cues.zh: 可以計算次序資料的變異數，但稍微……

cues.en: It can be a little bit weird.
cues.zh: 可能有點奇怪。

cues.en: So mostly variance is a sensible measure of dispersion for numerical data, and in particular data that are
cues.zh: 所以變異數主要是數值資料的合理離散程度量，尤其，

cues.en: more or less Gaussian distributed, unimodal distributed.
cues.zh: 大致高斯、單峰分布的資料。

cues.en: Okay, so here's a numeric example.
cues.zh: 看個數字例子。

cues.en: If you like, I encourage you to pause the video and apply this formula to compute the variance of this data set here.
cues.zh: 鼓勵暫停，套用公式，計算這個資料集的變異數。

cues.en: Okay, so again, the way we do that is by computing the mean of this data set, which turns out to be three, and then we subtract three from each one of these numbers.
cues.zh: 先算平均，結果是3，再從每個數減去3。

cues.en: So that gives us five, this turns into minus three, this turns into one and so on.
cues.zh: 得到5，這變成−3，這變成1，依此類推。

cues.en: And then each of these numbers individually gets squared.
cues.zh: 接著每個數分別平方。

cues.en: Slightly non-standard notation here.
cues.zh: 這裡記法稍微不標準。

cues.en: But each of these individual numbers get squared.
cues.zh: 但每個個別數都平方。

cues.en: And then we take the average of all of those squared differences from the mean, and that is our variance.
cues.zh: 再取所有與平均差距平方的平均，這就是變異數。

cues.en: And that turns out to be 16 for this particular dataset.
cues.zh: 這個資料集，結果是16。

cues.en: So now let's try this again.
cues.zh: 再試一次。

cues.en: Here's another numerical example.
cues.zh: 另一個數字例子。

cues.en: In this case, I have a dataset where the numbers are all closer to each other.
cues.zh: 這裡的數彼此更接近。

cues.en: So it's a two and two threes and three fours.
cues.zh: 一個2、兩個3、三個4。

cues.en: Again, if you like, you can pause the video and compute the variance applying this formula to this dataset.
cues.zh: 也可以暫停，套公式計算變異數。

cues.en: You'll get an answer of two thirds basically, 0.67.
cues.zh: 答案大致是三分之二，0.67。

cues.en: So it's pretty interesting to compare this variance to this variance.
cues.zh: 比較這兩個變異數很有意思。

cues.en: They're actually different by two orders of magnitude, although the numbers themselves don't differ by two orders of magnitude.
cues.zh: 相差兩個數量級，雖然數字本身沒差兩個數量級。

cues.en: In fact, the numbers here are in the same order of magnitude as these numbers, but the variance is two orders of magnitude off.
cues.zh: 這些數本身與前面的數，是同個數量級，但變異數差兩個數量級。

cues.en: So that was the...
cues.zh: 所以剛才的……

cues.en: The order of magnitude was 10, and here the order of magnitude is 0.1.
cues.zh: 數量級是10，這裡是0.1。

cues.en: So two orders of magnitude different from each other.
cues.zh: 彼此差兩個數量級。

cues.en: And basically what that means is that these numbers are all close together and the previous numbers were relatively far apart from each other.
cues.zh: 基本上代表，這些數很接近，前面的數相對分散。

cues.en: We can also visualize this on the number line.
cues.zh: 也能在數線上視覺化。

cues.en: So this is this first dataset and the second dataset, and I'm just plotting each of these values on the real number line here.
cues.zh: 這是第一個與第二個資料集，只把各個值畫在實數線。

cues.en: So what you see is that this one has a larger variance, this one has a small variance.
cues.zh: 這個變異數大，這個小。

cues.en: Here the data are more distributed.
cues.zh: 這裡資料比較分散。

cues.en: They go...
cues.zh: 它們……

cues.en: The spread is larger on the number line.
cues.zh: 在數線上展開範圍較大。

cues.en: And here the spread is very small on the number line.
cues.zh: 這裡範圍很小。

cues.en: In fact, there's even overlapping bars here that you don't see.
cues.zh: 其實有些長條重疊，所以看不到。

cues.en: Okay, so that's the formula, and I hope you also have an intuitive feel for variance.
cues.zh: 這就是公式，希望你也對變異數有直覺。

cues.en: Now I imagine that when you're looking at this formula, you have several questions about this formula and features in that formula.
cues.zh: 看到公式，你可能對公式與某些特徵有幾個問題。

cues.en: So I'm gonna try to read your mind and answer the questions that I imagine you might be thinking.
cues.zh: 讓我讀心，回答你可能在想的問題。

cues.en: The first question that maybe you're thinking is, why do we mean center?
cues.zh: 第一個，為什麼做平均中心化？

cues.en: Why do we have to subtract the mean?
cues.zh: 為什麼減去平均？

cues.en: And the answer to that is that we want the variance.
cues.zh: 因為我們要變異數。

cues.en: We want this measure to indicate the dispersion around the average and not so much about the absolute magnitude of the values themselves.
cues.zh: 希望衡量的是平均周圍的離散程度，而非數值本身的絕對大小。

cues.en: So for example, we want these two data sets to have the same measure of dispersion.
cues.zh: 例如，希望這兩個資料集，離散程度相同。

cues.en: We want them to have the same variance.
cues.zh: 希望變異數相同。

cues.en: Now these are...
cues.zh: 這些是……

cues.en: So these numbers are one, two, three, three, two, one.
And this is exactly the same number as I just added a 100 to all of them.
cues.zh: 另一組完全相同，只是每個都加100。

cues.en: Now, if you didn't mean center, the outcome of this formula, it's not the variance, but the outcome of the formula without subtracting the mean would be huge for this thing
cues.zh: 若不做平均中心化，公式結果雖不叫變異數，但不減平均的結果，這一組會非常大，

cues.en: because you're squaring all these 100 values and it would be pretty small for this one.
cues.zh: 因為把所有100多的值平方，另一組則很小。

cues.en: But you can see just by looking at these numbers that the dispersion is actually the same for both of these datasets.
cues.zh: 但只看數字，就知道兩組離散程度其實相同。

cues.en: It's just that dataset d2 is shifted on the real number line.
cues.zh: 只是d2在實數線上平移。

cues.en: It's shifted up by 99 or well by a 100 compared to dataset d1.
cues.zh: 相較d1，上移99，或者說100。

cues.en: So that's why we have to mean center.
cues.zh: 所以必須平均中心化。

cues.en: Okay, so then another question you might ask is, why are these differences squared?
cues.zh: 另一個問題，為什麼把差平方？

cues.en: Well, there's two ways to interpret this question.
cues.zh: 這個問題有兩種解讀。

cues.en: Why do we have to do anything?
cues.zh: 為什麼必須做其他事？

cues.en: Why can't we just subtract the mean and why is it squared and not something else?
cues.zh: 為什麼不能只減平均，還有為什麼平方，而非其他運算？

cues.en: Okay, so let me answer that first question first.
cues.zh: 先回答第一個。

cues.en: So the distances to the average...
cues.zh: 到平均的距離……

cues.en: So what we want to measure with variance is the distances of each number to the average.
cues.zh: 變異數要衡量每個數與平均之間的距離。

cues.en: And if we don't square then well, the variance, but it wouldn't be variance anymore.
cues.zh: 如果不平方，結果就不叫變異數了。

cues.en: But if we didn't square this term, if we drop this squared term, the outcome of this formula is always going to be zero.
cues.zh: 去掉平方，這個公式結果永遠是0。

cues.en: And we can see that with this simple example.
cues.zh: 簡單例子就能看出。

cues.en: If we mean center these data, then you can just see, you can just eyeball this and see that it's gonna sum to zero.
cues.zh: 把資料平均中心化，光看就知道，加總為0。

cues.en: And that's no surprise.
cues.zh: 不意外。

cues.en: When you mean center a data set and then you take the the new mean, well, the new mean is going to be zero because we've already subtracted the mean.
cues.zh: 平均中心化後再取新平均，它是0，因為已經減過平均。

cues.en: So that's why we need to have something here.
cues.zh: 所以需要在這裡加某個操作。

cues.en: Now you might say, well, you know, this doesn't need to be squared.
cues.zh: 你可能說，不一定平方吧。

cues.en: What if we would take the absolute value instead of squaring?
cues.zh: 改取絕對值如何？

cues.en: Well, it turns out you can do that.
cues.zh: 確實可以。

cues.en: So here I've modified this formula to give absolute value.
cues.zh: 這裡把公式改成絕對值。

cues.en: That is called the mean absolute difference if you adjust this formula to use absolute values instead of squares.
cues.zh: 把平方換絕對值，叫平均絕對差。

cues.en: So you might say, well, you know, why do we take the squares instead of the mean absolute difference?
cues.zh: 那為什麼取平方，不用平均絕對差？

cues.en: So the answer is that squaring emphasizes large values, which means that more spread out datasets will have a much larger variance.
cues.zh: 答案是，平方強調大數值，讓更分散的資料集，有大很多的變異數。

cues.en: And it turns out that squaring this just has a number of nicer properties.
cues.zh: 平方也有一些更好的性質。

cues.en: It's really good for optimization problems.
cues.zh: 很適合最佳化問題。

cues.en: And that's because when we square this term here, we have a function that is continuous and therefore differentiable.
cues.zh: 因為平方後，得到連續、因而可微的函數。

cues.en: So it's useful from a calculus perspective, whereas the mean absolute difference is not guaranteed to be a continuous, and therefore it's not guaranteed
cues.zh: 所以從微積分角度有用；平均絕對差不保證連續，也因此不保證，

cues.en: to be a differentiable function.
cues.zh: 是可微函數。

cues.en: So it can lead to some problems in optimization.
cues.zh: 可能在最佳化造成問題。

cues.en: And it's also closely related to Euclidean distance when we square this term to get variance.
cues.zh: 平方以得到變異數，也與歐幾里得距離密切相關。

cues.en: Closely related to Euclidean distance, it's also the second moment of the distribution.
cues.zh: 除了歐幾里得距離，也與分布的二階動差有關。

cues.en: I will define what this statistical moment means in, I guess, about half a dozen videos later on in this section.
cues.zh: 這一節大概再過六部影片，會定義統計動差。

cues.en: Squaring this difference also has a closer link to least-squares regression and basically just has a bunch of nice mathematical and statistical properties
cues.zh: 平方差也更密切連結最小平方法迴歸，基本上有很多良好的數學與統計性質，

cues.en: that make squaring the right thing to do.
cues.zh: 讓平方成為合適做法。

cues.en: Now of course, the mean absolute difference is also fine.
cues.zh: 當然，平均絕對差也沒問題。

cues.en: People use it sometimes.
cues.zh: 有時有人用。

cues.en: It is more robust to outliers, so it's less sensitive to outliers because we're not squaring terms here.
cues.zh: 對離群值更穩健、敏感度較低，因為沒有平方。

cues.en: So the variance is not going to...
cues.zh: 所以變異數不會……

cues.en: Or the mean absolute difference doesn't get really, really large with outliers the way that the variance would get really, really large with outliers.
cues.zh: 或者說，平均絕對差，不會像變異數一樣，被離群值拉得非常大。

cues.en: So this is also a perfectly good formula.
cues.zh: 所以這也是完全良好的公式。

cues.en: It's called mean absolute difference is closely related to another quantity called median absolute difference, which is actually a formula that I'm going to introduce you to
cues.zh: 叫平均絕對差，與另一個叫中位數絕對差的量密切相關，會介紹它的公式，

cues.en: in the section on outliers and cleaning your data.
cues.zh: 在離群值與資料清理那一節。

cues.en: So the conclusion here is that we square basically because it gives us a lot of nice properties that are useful in other applications of statistics and machine learning.
cues.zh: 結論是，平方帶來很多好性質，適用其他統計與機器學習應用。

cues.en: All right, and then the last question that I imagine you asking about this formula is why do we divide by n minus one instead of dividing by n?
cues.zh: 最後，你可能會問，為什麼除以n−1，而非n？

cues.en: Well, it turns out that dividing by n minus one is what's used to compute the sample variance, whereas dividing by n is used to compute the population variance.
cues.zh: 除以n−1，是計算樣本變異數；除以n，是計算母體變異數。

cues.en: So again, if you're being a real stickler for notation, you might use sigma squared for population variance and have that be one divided by n.
cues.zh: 非常嚴格的記法，可能用σ平方表示母體變異數，前面是1/n。

cues.en: And you might use S for our S squared for a sample variance, and then you would use n minus one.
cues.zh: 用S、或S平方表示樣本變異數，則用n−1。

cues.en: Again, most people are not so formal about using these common notations.
cues.zh: 再提醒，多數人不會這麼嚴格遵守常見記法。

cues.en: Okay, so the reason for this difference is that the population mean is a theoretical quantity, whereas the sample mean is an empirical quantity.
cues.zh: 這個差異，源於母體平均是理論量，樣本平均是經驗量。

cues.en: So the population mean is something that you can know in advance without necessarily measuring from the entire population.
cues.zh: 母體平均，可以事先知道，不一定要測量整個母體。

cues.en: Whereas the sample mean is an empirical quality.
cues.zh: 樣本平均則是經驗量。

cues.en: It's gonna differ for every single sample that you draw from a population, whereas the population mean doesn't change just because you're sampling from it.
cues.zh: 每次從母體抽樣會不同，母體平均卻不因抽樣而改變。

cues.en: So you know, a bunch of videos ago I discussed the population mean of height of Italians.
cues.zh: 很多部以前，談過義大利人身高的母體平均。

cues.en: So the average height of all Italians, that's a population mean.
cues.zh: 所有義大利人的平均身高，是母體平均。

cues.en: And that is the same, even if you're only measuring from one or two or 10 or even a 1000 Italians.
cues.zh: 即使只測一、二、十，甚至一千人，母體平均也相同。

cues.en: The population of Italians still has the same height regardless of how you're sampling them.
cues.zh: 不論怎麼抽樣，義大利人母體的身高仍然相同。

cues.en: But every sample of Italians that you measure is going to have a different height.
cues.zh: 但每個義大利人樣本，測得的身高會不同。

cues.en: It's gonna be...
cues.zh: 會是……

cues.en: You know, it should be close to the population mean, but it's gonna have its own empirical mean.
cues.zh: 應接近母體平均，但有自己的經驗平均。

cues.en: Okay, so let me give you an example of why this is the case.
cues.zh: 舉例說明原因。

cues.en: So the population mean of a die is 3.5.
cues.zh: 一顆骰子的母體平均是3.5。

cues.en: Now, I'm not encouraging anyone's fatality here.
cues.zh: 不是在鼓勵任何人死亡。

cues.en: A die is the singular of dice.
cues.zh: 英文die是dice的單數。

cues.en: It's the six-sided cube that you roll.
cues.zh: 就是擲的六面立方體。

cues.en: It has, you know, dots one through six on the six different sides.
cues.zh: 六個面分別有一到六個點。

cues.en: Okay, so the population mean of a die is 3.5.
cues.zh: 骰子的母體平均是3.5。

cues.en: That means if you take a die and or some dice and you roll them an infinite number of times and you take the average, the mean of all the faces
cues.zh: 意思是，拿一顆或幾顆骰子，擲無限次，再取所有點數的平均，

cues.en: that you would get after an infinite number of die rolls, you would get 3.5.
cues.zh: 無限次擲骰後，得到3.5。

cues.en: So that is the population mean.
cues.zh: 這是母體平均。

cues.en: Now I can take a die and roll it four times, and I'm not necessarily going to get an average of 3.5.
cues.zh: 但拿骰子擲四次，平均不一定是3.5。

cues.en: In this particular sample.
cues.zh: 在這個特定樣本，

cues.en: I might get an average of three, which is totally fine.
cues.zh: 可能平均是3，完全沒問題。

cues.en: That can happen.
cues.zh: 可能發生。

cues.en: Okay, and now here's the important question.
cues.zh: 重要問題來了。

cues.en: I roll the die four times and I tell you that the sample mean is three.
cues.zh: 擲四次，告訴你樣本平均是3。

cues.en: And I want you to tell me how many numbers you need to know to know all four values.
cues.zh: 要知道四個值，必須先知道幾個數？

cues.en: So I rolled the die four times.
cues.zh: 擲了四次。

cues.en: How many of those roles do you need to see in order to know all four of the values when I already told you that the sample mean is three?
cues.zh: 已知樣本平均3，還需要看其中幾次結果，才能知道全部四個？

cues.en: Now, if you don't already know the answer, feel free to pause the video and work through an example on a piece of paper with a pen or pencil.
cues.zh: 若還不知道，歡迎暫停，拿紙筆試個例子。

cues.en: So it turns out that the answer is you only need to know three of these roles.
cues.zh: 答案是只要知道三次。

cues.en: So for example, I tell you that the sample mean is three, and then I tell you that I rolled a one and a two and a four, and I don't tell you what the fourth role is.
cues.zh: 例如告訴你樣本平均3，擲出1、2、4，不告訴你第四次。

cues.en: I don't tell you that fourth value.
cues.zh: 不告訴你第四個值。

cues.en: I don't need to tell you that, you know what it has to be and it has to be five because this is the only unknown in this equation.
cues.zh: 也不需要告訴，因為它必須是5，這是方程式唯一未知數。

cues.en: And if that's not totally clear, then compute the average of these four numbers, set it equal to three.
cues.zh: 如果不清楚，就計算這四個數的平均，設成3。

cues.en: So it's basically one plus two plus four plus question mark divided by four equals three, and you'll be able to solve for question mark.
cues.zh: 基本上是(1+2+4+問號)/4=3，就能解出問號。

cues.en: So this means that there's actually only n minus one free values or also called degrees of freedom in this sample.
cues.zh: 表示樣本中只有n−1個自由值，也叫自由度。

cues.en: This other data point is not free, it is completely dependent on these other data points and on the mean.
cues.zh: 另一個資料點不自由，完全依賴其他點與平均。

cues.en: So once we know the mean and we know these other data points, there's always going to be one value that we don't need to know in advance because it is dependent on the other values and on the mean.
cues.zh: 知道平均與其他點後，永遠有一個值不需要事先知道，因為依賴其他值與平均。

cues.en: And that is why for a sample variance, we divide by n minus one.
cues.zh: 所以樣本變異數除以n−1。

cues.en: This is the number of degrees of freedom of this statistic.
cues.zh: 這是這個統計量的自由度。

cues.en: Alright, so that's all about variance.
cues.zh: 變異數到此。

cues.en: Now, I promised that I would spend less than 30 seconds talking about standard deviation.
cues.zh: 答應過，標準差要講不到30秒。

cues.en: So here goes.
cues.zh: 開始。

cues.en: Standard deviation is the square root of variance.
cues.zh: 標準差是變異數的平方根。

cues.en: So once you compute the variance, you take the standard deviation.
cues.zh: 所以算出變異數，再取標準差。

cues.en: And here I'm just, you know, giving a friendly little math reminder that the square root symbol is the same thing as taking a quantity to the power of one half.
cues.zh: 順便親切提醒，平方根符號，等於取某個量的二分之一次方。

cues.en: So there you go.
cues.zh: 就是這樣。

cues.en: Standard deviation is the square root of variance.
cues.zh: 標準差是變異數的平方根。

cues.en: That was around 23 seconds I think.
cues.zh: 大概23秒，我想。

cues.en: Okay, I very quickly wanna introduce you to the Fano factor and the coefficient of variation.
cues.zh: 快速介紹Fano因子與變異係數。

cues.en: I'm not gonna really talk about these too much, but they do appear in applications of statistics.
cues.zh: 不會談太多，但會出現在統計應用。

cues.en: For example, in physics, in computational biology, in neuroscience, you might come across these quantities.
cues.zh: 例如物理、計算生物、神經科學，可能看到。

cues.en: And essentially the Fano factor and the coefficient of variation are just normalized measures of variability.
cues.zh: 基本上，是經過正規化的變異程度量。

cues.en: So the Fano factor is variance divided by the mean, coefficient of variation is the standard deviation divided by the mean.
cues.zh: Fano因子是變異數除以平均，變異係數是標準差除以平均。

cues.en: These quantities are sensible only for data sets that have positive only values.
cues.zh: 這些量只適用全部正值的資料集。

cues.en: And you can imagine why that's the case by looking at the denominator.
cues.zh: 看分母就能想像原因。

cues.en: So imagine if you have a data set that's equally distributed around zero, then the mean is zero and then we're gonna be dividing by zero.
cues.zh: 若資料在0周圍均勻分布，平均是0，就會除以0。

cues.en: So Fano factor, coefficient of variation, these are normalized measures of variability and they're used for data sets that only contain positive values.
cues.zh: Fano因子、變異係數，是正規化的變異程度量，用於只有正值的資料集。

cues.en: Alright, so that's the end.
cues.zh: 到此結束。

cues.en: Congratulations.
cues.zh: 恭喜。

cues.en: You are now experts on the dominant measures of dispersion, which are really just variants and also standard deviation.
cues.zh: 現在你是主要離散程度量，也就是變異數與標準差的專家。

cues.en: But of course that's just the square root of variants.
cues.zh: 當然，標準差只是變異數的平方根。
